title: HB385 (2020 Regular): Firearms; require removal of for any person determined to be mentally ill.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2020/html/HB/0300-0399/HB0385IN.htm)
provenance.note: As-filed text; no passage vote recorded. Only subsection (6) is new; the rest of the civil-commitment section is unchanged.

operative_text: Section 1 (Miss. Code § 41-21-67): (6) Upon a determination under the provisions of this section, that a person is believed to be mentally ill, in need of treatment, poses an immediate substantial likelihood of physical harm to himself or herself or others, or is gravely disabled and unable to care for himself or herself by virtue of mental illness, the chancellor shall notify the chief law enforcement officer of the city or county in which such person resides for the purpose of determining whether the person owns any firearms, stun guns, pistols or revolvers. Upon notification by the chancellor, such chief law enforcement officer shall determine whether the person owns or has control over any firearms, stun guns, pistols or revolvers. If the chief law enforcement officer determines that the person does own or control any such firearms, stun guns, pistols or revolvers, such officer shall remove all firearms, stun guns, pistols or revolvers under the person's control.
